correctness.rationale: Analytically, removing area O(t^2) does not change the interior covariance to order t, while the boundary perimeter and central second moment change by (h-2)t and (h-2)(1+c)t/2, respectively. The resulting derivative is (h-2)(1+3c)/4. The explicit five-vertex convex example has integer edges and an independently reproduced exact rational positive excess 1521250837460015/1792478301783239474. The standalone Fraction checker was run successfully.

originality.rationale: Full texts of Tokmachev arXiv:2607.08869v1 and Lotnikov arXiv:2608.14848 were inspected for the random squared-chord statistics and implication directions. Their lower comparisons and symmetric-body formulas do not entail the claimed strict upper-amplification failure for an asymmetric pentagon. Separate indexed results on parallelogram fourth moments and triangle second moments are not statements implying this new first variation. Several targeted indexed and full-text searches found no equivalent. This is best-knowledge originality with genuine risk of unindexed prior work.
residual_risks: Unindexed classical geometric-probability sources may already prove this exact rhombus first variation or provide a general theorem implying it.
Relevant indexed published-finding corpus fourth-moment and triangle records were accessible as summaries but not full primary contents, so detailed undiscovered implications remain possible.
The result does not establish a global sharp upper bound or classify the zero first-variation angle.

value.rationale: Rhombi give the natural exact benchmark two, and the theorem identifies a sharp angular boundary separating local attenuation from amplification under a natural one-corner truncation. An exact integer-coordinate convex pentagon proves that the factor-two upper amplification intuition does not extend to all convex planar bodies; the mechanism is structurally meaningful for random chord-moment inequalities.
